title: Shot Metamorphosis — prompt morphing and brittle-case notes
content:
Purpose and rough goals:
- explore prompt "morphing" patterns: same semantic intent expressed across shapes (directive-to-story, terse-to-verbose), track failure modes when LLM flips intent or hallucinates details.
- build small library of few-shot exemplars that transfer across domain shifts (support/FAQ -> legal-summary -> code-explain).
- catalog brittle cases with short repros so other engineers can run quick A/B tests.

Notes to self (quick):
- keep fewshot sets small (3–5) for latency reasons but ensure coverage of edge tokens.
- try mixing instruction framing with a persona line vs. adding example that demonstrates persona; sometimes persona line causes stubbornness.
- test with temperature 0.0 / 0.2 / 0.7 to characterize deterministic vs. creative failure.

Experiments done (high-level):
1) Template morph A -> B -> C (same intent: "summarize policy change for end users")
   - A (directive): "Summarize the policy change below in 3 bullet points for our customers. Keep it under 60 words."
   - B (story): "Imagine you're a product manager announcing a small policy change. Write a short announcement in plain English with three bullets and a friendly closing."
   - C (Q/A priming): "Q: What changed? A: ..." then provide summarization.
   Observations: B yields more empathetic phrasing but occasionally omits the core technical caveat present in the source. C forces explicit structure but sometimes repeats source wording verbatim (bad for paraphrase).

2) Few-shot exemplar set: "concise-summary" family (3-shot)
   - Ex1 (good): Input: long legal statute; Output: 3 bullets, each 10-14 words, avoid legalese.
   - Ex2 (warn): Input: changelog entry with code example; Output: include code fence and clear example mapping.
   - Ex3 (edge): Input: ambiguous timeframe; Output: ask clarifying question unless instruction says to assume.
   Result: Model mostly follows style, but when input includes lists and enumerations in the source, it tends to carry over numbering formatting. Need post-processing to normalize.

Failure cases observed (short repros):
- Failure: model invents compliance exceptions when source says 'no exceptions'.
  Repro: supply source paragraph with phrase "no exceptions will be made"; prompt: "Summarize in 2 bullets for customers".
  Symptom: output bullet adds an exception clause like "except for X".
  Hypothesis: probabilistic overcorrection to soften absolute statements.
  Mitigation attempts: add explicit constraint in prompt: "Do not add exceptions or qualifications not present in the text." Mixed results.

- Failure: temporal drift — model rewrites dates to localized timezone (e.g., March 5 -> March 4 PST).
  Repro: policy change with UTC timestamp; ask for short summary.
  Mitigation: canonicalize dates in input to ISO and add explicit rule: "Do not change dates." Works at low temp.

- Failure: persona leakage — when persona example includes phrases like "as your friendly PM" model injects similar voice into factual code-explains causing informal tone.
  Repro: include a friendly exemplar in few-shot + a code snippet.
  Note: sometimes desirable for customer-facing text, but bad for API docs.

Prompt recipes to try next (quick list):
- "Constrained paraphrase shell": Instruction + required tokens list + forbidden tokens list. E.g., "Must include: 'effective date'. Must not use: 'exception', 'unless'".
- "Meta-exemplar selection": dynamically pick the one exemplar whose intent vector (via embedding) is closest to the input. See linked GitHub prototype.
- "Ask-before-summarize" toggle: if input ambiguity score > threshold, have model return clarifying question instead of summary. Need example of clarifying Qs in prompt.

Mini-protocol for systematic logging of brittle cases (for SRE/QA handoff):
- minimal repro input (<=2 paragraphs)
- exact prompt used (including system/prefix)
- model config (model name, temp, max tokens)
- expected pattern vs actual output and error category (hallucination / omission / tone / formatting)
- one-line mitigation tried and result
This doc should contain several of these records for quick triage.

Short checklist for experiments (copy for future runs):
- [ ] create canonical inputs with edge tokens: 'no exceptions', ISO dates, nested lists, legal terms, code fences
- [ ] run each input with T in {0.0, 0.2, 0.6}, top_p in {0.9, 1.0}
- [ ] include 'forbid' list in 50% of runs, persona exemplar in 50% of runs
- [ ] capture embeddings distances for exemplar selection runs
- [ ] produce summary table (CSV) with failure counts by category

Quick prototypes in this file (copy-paste to runner):
- Proto 1 (strict two-bullet):
  "Instruction: Summarize the text below in exactly two bullets. Each bullet must be 8–15 words. Do not add information not present."
  Example: (insert source)

- Proto 2 (clarify-or-summarize):
  "If the input is ambiguous about who is affected or when, respond with a clarifying question instead of a summary. Otherwise produce a 3-bullet summary."

- Proto 3 (persona toggled):
  "You are an empathetic support rep. Summarize in plain language for non-technical customers. Avoid legal phrasing. If the source contains an explicit ban, mark it clearly as 'No exceptions.'"

Open questions / hypotheses: (for A/B design)
- Q1: Does adding a short contrast exemplar (good vs bad) improve adherence more than adding 2 good exemplars? Hypothesis: contrast reduces token-level ambiguity and reduces hallucination.
- Q2: Is it better to forbid tokens (explicit blacklist) or to give positive must-have tokens? Hypothesis: forbids are stronger but brittle; must-haves help structure.
- Q3: Does temperature interact with persona presence differently across families of prompts? Need factorial experiment.

Operational notes for sharing with SEs:
- The smallest reproducible examples are easiest to communicate to customers. Keep examples < 200 tokens.
- When packaging a prompt recipe for the console, expose toggles: temperature, persona_on (bool), enforce_token_constraints (bool), clarify_threshold (float).

TODO (short):
- [ ] add 6 minimal repros into separate files in /shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/experiments/ (ask Lena to create folder)
- [ ] wire the proto prompts into the prompt-catalog runner and add a test matrix script (tag: INF-2098)
- [ ] sanity-check phrase blacklist vs must-have tokens across models (gpt-ish and open variants)
- [ ] write a short internal note summarizing three high-risk patterns for customers (hallucinate-exceptions, date-drift, persona-leak)

Random micro-observations (scratch):
- when the source is a bullet list, the model sometimes double-bullets — converts 1-level list into nested bullets. Post-normalize by collapsing bullets starting with numbers.
- adding an initial line: "Do not invent facts" is helpful but not sufficient. Better: "If you are not certain, say 'uncertain' and ask for clarification."
- short exemplars (<20 words) sometimes bias output to be terse even when instruction said verbose. Keep exemplar length aligned with target style.

Notes to future-me: paste this into the console notes and mark results as WIP. If we see >1 hallucination per 10 samples, consider adding a verification step using an extraction model to check for contradictions.

End of scratchpad.

-- Asha
